advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test asserting a commit-message file in a per-session subdirectory of /tmp or /var/tmp is NOT refused by the shared-scratch guard.
evidence: Guard uses parent equality: `return absolute.parent in _SHARED_SCRATCH_ROOTS` (scripts/amend_commit_message.py:94), so subdirectory acceptance is a distinct code path with no covering test.
ABSENCE: no test constructs a path like `/tmp/<unique>/msg.txt` and asserts it passes the guard (or is only rejected for not existing).

The only added test asserts refusal of `module._read_message_file("/tmp/commitmsg.txt")` (test_amend_msg_change_id.py:331); no test asserts a subdirectory path like `/tmp/session-abc/commitmsg.txt` is NOT refused.

CONTRIBUTING.md / AGENTS.md added text tells authors to use a per-session/per-invocation unique directory — a common such directory is under /tmp — so allow-under-/tmp-subdir is the intended happy path and is untested.
Ticket 919d-7994 disposition: 'unique mktemp/template and ticket-stamped directories left alone' — that allow-case is the behavior needing a regression anchor.
scripts/amend_commit_message.py:55-57: `_SHARED_SCRATCH_ROOTS = { root for path in (Path("/tmp"), Path("/var/tmp")) ... }`
The only refusal test uses `/tmp/commitmsg.txt`; `search_files` for `var/tmp` in the test file returns no matches.
Named violating input the added lines must reject but no test drives: `/var/tmp/commitmsg.txt`.
advisory.finding: The new guard is tested only for the rejection case (`/tmp/commitmsg.txt`); there is no test asserting that a commit-message file in a per-session SUBDIRECTORY of a shared root (e.g. `/tmp/session-x/msg.txt`) is ACCEPTED. This is the exact boundary the change relies on — an over-broad guard rejecting subdirectories would still pass the added test.
merged_from: No test verifies that a commit-message file in a per-session/unique subdirectory of a shared scratch root (e.g. `/tmp/session-abc/commitmsg.txt`) is ACCEPTED. This is the guard's core discriminator (`absolute.parent in _SHARED_SCRATCH_ROOTS` — only DIRECT children are refused). A regression that widened the check to reject any `/tmp`-descendant would break the documented recommended workflow (mktemp -d under /tmp) yet pass every existing test.
The guard explicitly adds `/var/tmp` as a shared scratch root, but no test exercises a `/var/tmp/...` path. The `/var/tmp` branch of `_SHARED_SCRATCH_ROOTS` is entirely unverified.

dropped.finding: The `RuntimeError` fallback path in `_is_direct_shared_scratch_file` uses `.absolute()`, which does not resolve `..` or symlinks, so on platforms where `/tmp` is a symlink (e.g. macOS `/private/tmp`) a path expressed via a symlinked or dotted form could bypass the guard in the fallback branch; the branch is also untested.
